From: Anika Bose <anika@skyline.ai>

Subject: Question: multi-region billing and per-token discounts

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — Skyline is seriously interested in Redwood for our inference layer. Before we get our procurement and finance teams engaged, I need to clarify how your hosted pricing would look for a global deployment. A few specifics:

- We expect ~1.2B tokens/month total in Q1, rising to ~3.5B by Q3.
- Estimated regional split: US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15%.
- We need predictable per-token unit economics; interested in commit tiers/discounts and how cross-region requests are billed.
- EU residency is important for a subset of requests (can you confirm data residency options and any pricing deltas?).
- Any additional surcharges for APAC egress/region-specific capacity?

Can you send a succinct options matrix (pay-as-you-go, committed tier, hybrid reserved + hosted fallback) and an example of blended token pricing across regions? Also: timeline and standard SLA uplift/add-ons for reserved pools.

Appreciate it — Anika

---
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Anika Bose <anika@skyline.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: multi-region billing and per-token discounts

Hi Anika — great to meet you as well. High level answers below; I attached a short pricing matrix and a draft SOW so you have something concrete to share internally.

1) Pricing primitives we use:
   - PAYG (hosted): per-token unit price by model family; billed in the region where the request was served.
   - COMMIT (reserved monthly tokens): bucketed token commit with stepped discounts at breakpoints (e.g., 250M, 1B, 2.5B tokens).
   - DEDICATED (reserved capacity): fixed monthly fee + lower per-token rate inside dedicated pool.

2) Cross-region behavior:
   - Requests served out of a region incur that region's unit price.
   - When you have a global commit, we offer a blended allocation option where committed tokens are deducted from a global bucket and then we apply a small region weighting surcharge for APAC (typically 3%–7% depending on burst capacity). EU residency requests can be pinned to EU-hosted endpoints (no cross-region billing) — that option typically maps to a slightly higher committed rate because capacity is reserved.

3) Example approach for Skyline (draft):
   - Option A: Global monthly commit 1B tokens — blended rate = $0.0036/token (after 15% discount), APAC uplift +5% if served outside reserved APAC pool.
   - Option B: Hybrid — EU-dedicated commit for 300M tokens @ $0.0038/token; remaining global commit 700M @ blended $0.0037. Pay-as-you-go for burst beyond commit, with regional PAYG rates.

4) SLA / burst & reserved capacity:
   - Dedicated pools come with IOPS & latency SLAs and a guaranteed baseline throughput. Hosted fallback if dedicated reaches capacity (optional — we can bill fallback at PAYG or a slightly higher overflow rate).

I'll loop in Lauren (Sales Ops) and Karthik (Finance) to produce a short matrix with concrete per-token numbers by region and a sample invoice/line-item view.

Best,

Looping in Lauren (Sales Ops) and Karthik (Finance) — both can provide the detailed matrix and invoice examples. Quick notes on the EU residency and APAC uplift:

- EU residency: we can pin endpoints and route traffic to EU-only hosting. That configuration requires a small capacity reservation (we treat it like a mini-dedicated pool) which is reflected as a modest increase in the committed per-token rate because of the region pinning. No cross-region billing for pinned requests.
- APAC uplift: default approach is blended commit with a region uplift applied at the serving time. If Skyline prefers predictable APAC behavior, we can provision a small reserved APAC pool (monthly fee + lower per-token inside pool) and configure automatic burst-to-hosted fallback.

I've attached the matrix with three scenarios (PAYG, Global Commit, Hybrid with EU pinning + APAC reserve) and a sample invoice layout. Lauren — can you call out the blended math and any one-time onboarding/setup fees? Karthik — any opt-out rules we should surface (e.g., minimum commit term, early termination credit rules)?

Thanks — Priyom

Hi Anika — I pulled the numbers into a simple matrix (see attached pricing-matrix-20261122.xlsx). Summary highlights and a short worked example below: 

- Baseline PAYG rates (hosted): US $0.0045/token, EU $0.0049/token, APAC $0.0052/token.
- Commit breakpoints we typically use: 250M (5% discount), 1B (15% discount), 2.5B+ (25% discount). Discounts apply to the committed bucket only.
- Blended global commit math example (1B commit):
   * Weighted regional base = US(55%*$0.0045) + EU(30%*$0.0049) + APAC(15%*$0.0052) = $0.00466/token
   * Apply commit discount (15%) => $0.00396/token 
   * APAC uplift (if served from non-reserved APAC capacity) = +5% => $0.00416/token for those tokens.
- EU pinned requests: when pinned to EU pool they are billed at the EU reserved rate (no cross-region billing).
- Overages/burst: PAYG overage = regional PAYG rate; optional overflow billing at PAYG + 10% if you want preferred capacity access.

Other commercial items:
- One-time onboarding & capacity provisioning fee: $12,500 (waivable with 12-month commit).
- Minimum commit term for discounted commit tiers: 3 months (we prorate monthly).
- Early termination: credit for unused committed tokens at 60% of the committed per-token price when terminated before term.

I uploaded a DocuSign link for the SOW in the matrix and added a sample invoice layout showing line items (commit tokens, reserved pool fee, regional surcharges, onboarding). Link: https://docusign.com/embedded?token=ABC1234-SKYLINE-SOW

If this looks good, next steps would be: 1) confirm target commit level and EU pinned volume, 2) sign SOW, 3) we provision reserved pools (2–3 business days for EU baseline), 4) test routing and warm KV caches.

Best,
